tagline: River towns and canal traces along the western Adirondack edge
intro: The Black River Trail follows the western edge of the Adirondack wilderness in the Adirondack Regional Tourism Council’s guide. NYSDOT describes its scenic byway as lesser-traveled highways through a valley between the Tug Hill Plateau and the Adirondacks, recognizing scenic and historic qualities. The two accounts cover different ground: the tourism guide connects Ogdensburg and Rome; NYSDOT’s 94-mile corridor connects Rome and Dexter on Lake Ontario.

Water carried traffic before this became a scenic drive: the Black River Canal was built to connect with the Erie Canal. At Lyons Falls, the village stood at the canal’s northern end when it was completed in 1858. The canal closed in 1924; seven of its locks form a historic district at Boonville Gorge Park.

Taking the tourism guide’s corridor south, begin at Ogdensburg on the St. Lawrence, then pass through Gouverneur, Harrisville and Croghan to Lowville. Continue to Lyons Falls, where the Black River drops 70 feet over gneiss, and onward to Rome.

moments.title: Ogdensburg
moments.text: Ogdensburg stands where the Oswegatchie meets the St. Lawrence, with the only U.S. port on the St. Lawrence Seaway. Its role as a trading city expanded in the mid-19th century as railroads developed across northern New York and southeastern Canada. Another transport connection followed in 1960, when the Ogdensburg-Prescott International Bridge linked the city with Johnstown, Ontario. Downtown, the Frederic Remington Art Museum occupies industrialist David Parish’s former mansion on Washington Street, where Eva Remington lived after her husband’s death.

moments.title: Lowville
moments.text: Lowville’s name honors landowner Nicholas Low; it does not describe the elevation or the cattle on nearby dairy farms. The farming connection is real, though: fertile soil on the Black River Flats helped agriculture and dairying flourish. The village became the county seat in 1864, succeeding Martinsburg. Its Civil War monument, built in 1883, is made of sand-cast zinc. A soldier tops the 20-foot structure, above a column and a three-stepped base.

moments.title: Lyons Falls
moments.text: At Lyons Falls, the Moose River joins the Black River from the east just above a 70-foot drop over a gneiss cliff. The village also marked the northern end of the Black River Canal when it was completed in 1858. Along the Black River, steep upper and lower reaches supplied mechanical power for mills and later hydroelectricity, while the middle 40 miles have practically no gradient. The river flows north through Lyons Falls; most of the village lies on its west bank, in West Turin.
